claim: The promoted LIVE cases (LIVE-01, LIVE-02, LIVE-03, LIVE-04, LIVE-05, LIVE-06, LIVE-07, LIVE-08, LIVE-09, LIVE-10) are exercised against the production `noble live repl` child built from this committed tree. LIVE-01: a resident V8 reload whose ACK precedes a fresh next top-level stack, with the same worker child PID observed before the first submission and after the ACK. LIVE-02: Decision 21a's post-ACK script derives the declared [24, 21] from the retained old Program's captured 21 and the rebuilt dependent's 24, and the same source, flags and `[ addone ]` submission are additionally held in flight at the feature seam so the reload ACK is observed only after that frame returns on its old generation. LIVE-03: every declared replacement is refused at admission with the old definition still callable, including the host-binding-mismatch variant run as written (startup manifest binding, replacement module, admission refusal, generation and stack preserved, next `addone` = 8). LIVE-04: ten canonical-section-edited variants of the captured emission each stop at an exact expected class - the four Noble-policy and three invalid variants in the worker's own byte validator or V8 at stage `wasm`, the forged-digest, independent-digest and oversized variants at shipped host byte admission - with the worker's memory, table, globals, guest-execution and host-request witness unchanged and the installed `base` still returning 7. LIVE-05: a resident V8 `noble live watch` child publishes only the complete atomic save (the next call returns 22) and leaves the prior generation unchanged for a partial in-place write, a symlink escape and the retained-generation budget refusal, and the shipped `noble live repl --allow-effects test.emit,test.abort` trap keeps the request prefix [test.emit:A, test.abort] and terminates the session; its `missing-import` variant is dropped as inapplicable (owner decision 30). LIVE-06: a retained old Program whose request is denied under the revoked current host policy. LIVE-07: an explicit interpreter choice refused at startup without a V8 fallback. LIVE-08: under integrator decision 42's `--require-proof addone` policy, the old definition's accepted evidence presented for `def addone [ 2 + ]` is refused by the core's correspondence check and the old source's emitted bytes replayed for the new candidate are refused against the host's own emission, both at admission with generation 1, the stack and the worker arena unchanged, after which fresh evidence publishes generation 2 (`20 addone` = 22) while the retained `[ addone ]` still returns 21; staged evidence is consumed by each attempt and other definitions stay proof-optional. LIVE-09: two real V8 guests that observe generation 1, queue a typed pure Program during the callback, publish input-dependent derived definitions at generation 2 whose committed source digests are the re-accepted derived texts, show the worker's cumulative guest-execution counter identical across invocation, pending and committed receipts, show the grant still selected after two refused dependents and null after the successful publication, and refuse an effect-increasing file restore. Byte substitution, the in-flight hold and proposal tampering are named `live-test-barrier` seams; their default-binary absence is observed separately. LIVE-10: under integrator decision 41 every remaining origin, rearm, callback-denial, post-return-refusal and terminal-trap variant is observed: with a grant for another name the self words are refused at source admission, a foreign-session grant is not representable (dropped), and the shadow-stage failure and the generation change between enqueue and publication run under one-shot `live-test-barrier` fault models, each refusing before publication with the grant and stack kept and the next proposal committing. No proof and no case outside the promoted set is claimed.

non_claims: No Lean/Aeneas/Verus proof, translation validation or refinement claim is made; every promoted case keeps proof open.

LIVE-02 is promoted from same-input evidence: the plain child runs the case source, flags and submissions, and the `live-repl` feature child holds the identical `[ addone ]` submission at the `in-flight-execution` seam. OWNER DECISION 2026-11-20 (Decision 21a) replaced the case's `after_reload_ack` script; the decision is recorded in the change tasks and here, not in the case `input`.

LIVE-03's `incompatible-schema` variant is refused as a second declaration of the same module version, before any opaque-schema comparison; the case reject outcome and the preserved session are observed, a distinct schema diagnostic is not claimed. Its `missing-module` and `effect-ceiling-increase` replacements are refused lexically or as unbound words, and `changed-file-during-read` rests on the named feature-gated real-child test.

LIVE-05's `missing-import` variant is dropped as inapplicable (owner decision 30: the live profiles have no import grammar, so `import missing@1 as m` is refused lexically before any import resolution); no missing-registry check is claimed. The trap variant runs in the shipped `noble live repl` under the explicit host grant (Decision 22), not under the watched-session harness, and `test.emit` is a Core host effect request that performs no Declared-Modules protected operation, so its measured `protected_operations` is 0.

LIVE-04 observations use the `live-test-barrier` byte seam only to serve the mutated bytes and, for the independent-digest variant, to present a digest; the decisions are the shipped worker byte validator/Noble policy checks and the shipped host source/binding/frame admission compiled into every binary. A default binary with every seam variable set executed normally and wrote no capture (observed absence).

LIVE-09's ordinary `run`/`session` rows are the same committed default binary and Core-Bootstrap profile; they observe that the live self-edit words remain unbound outside the live REPL, not a temporal comparison with an older binary.

LIVE-10's shadow-stage failure and generation change between enqueue and publication are test-only fault models of the feature build (integrator decision 41): the serial live host admits a proposal right after the invocation returns, so no CLI input reaches either; the shipped binary has neither selection. A foreign-session grant is not representable and is dropped; with a grant for another name the self words are refused at source admission.

LIVE-08 runs the bounded proof-required profile of integrator decision 42 (`--require-proof NAME`, one dependency-free `def NAME [ BODY ]` subject, evidence staged by `:evidence`): the Lean recheck is the shared `noble build --require-proof` consumer with the reviewed sandbox tools and the tested tree's `proofs/mc1` library, the claim is about the candidate body as a closed quotation subject, and its replayed-bytecode variant serves the old source's emitted bytes through the existing `live-test-barrier` byte seam. It is not a translation, refinement or Wasm-correspondence proof.
The interpreter refusal is an observed refusal, not a proof that no custom bytecode ISA exists anywhere.

The gate observes single bounded child sessions; it does not claim filesystem-watch completeness or V8 garbage collection. Binaries are retained under `bin/`: build hashes depend on the output path, so `binary_sha256` is confirmable against the retained copy rather than by rebuilding elsewhere.
